summary: Closed the end-to-end limitation on the conf-change finding. The earlier network attempt dropped the malformed change because the pending-conf guard fired: that harness never advanced the application's applied index. The harness now acknowledges applied entries the way Advance does (raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on every peer) after each application applies the joint change, then proposes the empty JointExplicit change on the real three-node leader. A local run shows the guard cleared (pendingConfIndex 2, applied 2, already_pending false), the malformed change accepted as EntryConfChangeV2 at index 3, that index committed (committed 3, committed_reached true), and applying it panicking with config is already joint while still joint - so the malformed change does reach the application through a genuine commit. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation with a prerequisite on the cleared guard and three comparisons (entry_type EntryConfChangeV2, committed_reached true, panicked true), plus the existing facts as knowledge uses; the asserted claim is unchanged and this removes its most consequential limitation, leaving only that appliedTo stands in for the Ready and Advance path in the harness.
